headline: High risk: n8n’s server-side write/network capabilities can amplify caveman outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while n8n can read/write server files and execute workflow nodes. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if n8n ingests caveman-authored text or files. The exact bridge is undocumented, so I choose medium over low because shared file surfaces make injection feasible by default.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest caveman-generated files or notes as prompts
IF a shared filesystem path is used between the two agents
IF workflow nodes parse caveman output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict n8n to a separate workspace directory
Add a prompt-injection filter before any n8n AI node
Require explicit human review for caveman-authored files before workflow use
Disable MCP access for caveman in shared environments
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and n8n consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and has broad network egress. If those data classes enter n8n workflows, they can be transmitted to external integrations. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default n8n setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF caveman project notes or session logs are passed into an n8n workflow
IF an n8n integration node sends workflow payloads to a third-party service
IF shared files contain secrets or sensitive project context
mitigations: Keep caveman logs and notes out of n8n input paths
Use a redaction step before any n8n API node
Limit n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists in workflow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes project files, while n8n supports multiple instances with shared state via datastore and connected systems plus server filesystem access. Even though n8n does not modify git state, overlapping writes to shared files or workflow state can race and corrupt outputs. The conflict is real in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF multiple n8n executions run concurrently on shared state
IF caveman and n8n target the same project files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared files
Use file locks or queueing around shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent runs on the same workspace
requires-engineering: add transactional state management for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that n8n can ingest through filesystem or workflow inputs, and n8n can then execute commands or integrations based on that content. Because n8n has action-taking authority and broad egress, a mistaken or malicious caveman output can cascade into irreversible external actions. This is a default-danger pathway, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n uses caveman output as authoritative workflow input
IF an n8n workflow triggers Execute Command or external integrations from that input
IF no verification step exists between caveman output and n8n actions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any n8n action node
Require human approval for command or API execution
Constrain n8n workflows to read-only dry runs first
Log and review caveman-to-n8n handoffs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for all upstream text

E_compliance.rationale: caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while n8n processes arbitrary workflow data on its server and handles credentials per credential store. If regulated data enters n8n, retention and residency obligations can diverge from caveman’s local project artifacts. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through n8n workflows
IF caveman project files contain data subject to retention or deletion rules
IF n8n credentials or logs retain data longer than the source workspace
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into n8n
Set short retention on workflow logs
Avoid placing regulated data in caveman project files
Review n8n credential and execution log retention
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion policies across both systems
